chunks: From him, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Rabi' ibn Abdullah, from Al-Fudayl, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent down the Ajwa and the Ateeq from the sky. I said, 'And what is the Ateeq?' He said, 'The stallion.'

key_terms.الْعَتِيق: Al-Ateeq (the stallion, specifically a mature male camel or horse)
key_terms.الْعَجْوَة: Ajwa (a specific type of high-quality date, or potentially a specific animal breed in this context)

ai.seo_question: What does the term 'Al-Ateeq' refer to in Shia hadith literature?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) identifies 'Al-Ateeq' as the stallion (specifically the male camel or horse), highlighting the divine origin of premium sustenance and prized livestock. This reflects the Shia scholarly understanding of 'Al-Ateeq' as a term of excellence, linking the celestial blessing of the Ajwa date with the nobility of the stallion, both symbolizing high quality and divine favor in material blessings.

en.hubeali:
From him, from his father, form Hammad Bin Isa, from Rabie Bin Abdullah, from Al Fuzayl, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Sent down Al-Ajwa and Al-Ateeq from the sky’. I said, ‘And what is Al-Ateeq?’ Heasws said: ‘The stallion’.
en.sarwar: 9. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from his father from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Rib‘iy from ‘Abd Allah ibn al- Fudayl who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, sent al-‘Ajwah and al-‘Atiq from the sky.’ I then asked, ‘What is al-‘Atiq ?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It is the male.’”
